title: Sarnath
subtitle: A first-teaching tradition and later Buddhist pilgrimage site
timeLabel: Early Buddhist tradition through the site's first-millennium development; modern conservation continues
shortSummary: Sarnath connects Śākyamuni, the first-turning-of-the-Dharma tradition, early monastic memory and later Buddhist pilgrimage to a real archaeological place.
curatorialDescription: The real map shows a geographic reference for the archaeological site; the claim that the Buddha first taught here belongs to a layered history of texts, tradition and heritage memory.
The place record does not treat surviving monuments as a literal scene from the fifth century BCE. Teaching tradition, archaeological remains and modern conservation remain separate layers.
researchNote: The coordinate is a site-level schematic point. The first-teaching narrative comes from early Buddhist texts and later heritage memory; architectural phases and pilgrimage history still require periodisation.
